findings.claim: The new --shout flag has no test: nothing checks that `greet.sh --shout ada` prints `HELLO ADA`, or that the default path still prints `hello ada` after the rewrite.
findings.suggestion:
In tests/greet_test.sh, run the script as a CLI and compare its exact output, e.g.
  [ "$(sh "$(dirname "$0")/../bin/greet.sh" --shout ada)" = 'HELLO ADA' ]
  [ "$(sh "$(dirname "$0")/../bin/greet.sh" ada)" = 'hello ada' ]
and also `--shout` with no name (expect `HELLO WORLD`).

findings.claim: The only test can't fail: `|| :` swallows the script's failure and `[ -n x ] || [ -z x ]` is always true, so `sh tests/run.sh` passes whatever greet.sh does, this change included.
findings.suggestion: Drop the `|| :` and assert the exact output: `out=$(sh "$(dirname "$0")/../bin/greet.sh" ada)` then `[ "${out}" = 'hello ada' ]`.
findings.out_of_scope: The test came from the earlier commit 087a01f, not this MR; it matters here because it is the only check of the rewritten output path.

noticed.text: Switching from printf to `echo "${line}"` makes sh interpret backslashes in the name: `greet.sh 'a\tb'` now prints a real tab (checked on macOS /bin/sh). That is a regression on the default path; `printf '%s\n' "${line}"` keeps the old behaviour.
`tr a-z A-Z` uppercases ASCII only, so names with accents stay lower case (shellcheck SC2018/SC2019); `tr '[:lower:]' '[:upper:]'` handles them.

notes.text: `[ "${1-}" = --shout ] && { ...; }` is safe under `set -eu`: the false test on the left of `&&` doesn't trip `set -e`, and `${1-}` avoids the unset error when there are no arguments.
